effect: The fish strip is coloured and ready to try in the drum.
reaction: Colouring was straightforward; I’m curious to see the pictures move.
reason: The completed picture strip belongs inside the turning drum.
expectation: The strip should fit inside the drum for viewing through its slits.

effect: The coloured strip is installed in the drum, ready to be viewed.
reaction: I'm curious whether the slits will make the fish appear to move.
reason: The lantern is the remaining item and should illuminate the pictures inside the drum.
expectation: The light should make the fish sequence visible as the drum turns.

effect: The lantern completed the drum and showed how brief views through the slits turn separate drawings into apparent motion; reversing the drum reverses the sequence.
reaction: The contrast between the blurred view and the moving fish through the slits was satisfying and informative.

mostWorthwhile.text: Finishing and viewing the animation drum was most worthwhile: it connected the drawings to a clear demonstration of how the slits make motion visible.

leastWorthwhile.text: Colouring the strip was straightforward but added little to my understanding compared with building the sequence and viewing it.

surprise.text: Reversing the drum made the splash seem to gather back into a fish, showing that the sequence works backwards too.

arbitrary.text: The stencil's exact role was not obvious at first, though the result explained that it helped make the in-between poses.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the animation mechanism was worth exploring, and the idea of a whale carrying the stalls makes me curious about the next construction.
